subject: Locking GPUs for Production: Sync & Technical Deep‑Dive Availability
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@vertexsys.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@vertexsys.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-16T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Locking GPUs for Production: Sync & Technical Deep‑Dive Availability

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery: Vertex is planning an initial 2-node dedicated GPU pool to support a customer-facing summarization workflow (GPT-style family) with peak concurrency around 18 sessions and an expected sustained QPS that maps to ~80 prompt tokens/sec aggregate. Your initial target is an operational p95 latency sub-400ms on the 1k token window for the primary model.

Next steps we proposed on the call:
- Schedule a 45-minute technical deep-dive (throughput + latency targets + model artifact exchange)
- Share any production traffic samples or a short profile (attached) so we can size batch / cache configs
- Identify a 2-week pilot window and smoke-test topology (can be hosted Dedicated or Private)

Can you please share 2–3 windows in the next 7 business days for the tech call? I’m including Rishi and Monica on thread — Rishi will lead the sizing portion and Monica will coordinate the pilot contract terms.

Attachments: vertex_production_profile.xlsx (sample traffic + SLA targets)

Calendly link if easier to pick a time: https://calendly.com/redwood-lauren/tech-deep-dive-30m

Best,

—Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0198

Thanks Lauren — appreciated the summary and the attached profile.

We can do the deep-dive next week. Available slots (PT):
- Tue 2026-10-20: 10:00–10:45 or 15:30–16:15
- Wed 2026-10-21: 09:30–10:15
- Thu 2026-10-22: 13:00–13:45

Priya and I will bring our infra lead (Samir) for the throughput discussion; Samir will want to review the KV cache/latency tradeoffs. We’ll also upload a small set of representative production traces to the Drive link you shared.

Also: to confirm the must-haves from our end — we need predictable P95, regional placement in us-west-2, and an option to burst to additional GPUs for Black Friday traffic.

Alex

Subject: Re: Locking GPUs for Production: Sync & Technical Deep‑Dive Availability

Alex — thanks for the options. Let’s lock Tue 2026-10-20 10:00–10:45 PT. I’ve booked a provisional invite; you should see a calendar event from "Redwood Meetings". Attendees: Lauren (SE), Rishi (Performance), Monica (CS/Contract).

Prep items for the call (Rishi / Monica, FYI):
- Rishi: bring a shorthand sizing worksheet that maps token throughput -> GPU model/core count and a couple quantization scenarios. We likely need a 2-node baseline with a 1.5x burst option.
- Monica: prepare a short pilot SOW bullet list (30–60 day objectives + SLIs).
- Alex / Priya / Samir: if possible, upload one hour of production traces (anonymized) to the Drive link before Mon EOD so we can precompute batching recommendations.

I’m attaching a short Redwood Dedicated FAQ (redwood_dedicated_faq.pdf) that answers common questions about region pinning, private control-plane options, and encryption-at-rest.

See you Tuesday — I’ll share dial-in and a short agenda before the call.

—Lauren

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_faq.pdf

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Prep for Vertex technical deep-dive (Tue 10/20)

Internal note —

Short checklist before Tuesday’s call:
1) Rishi: produce two quick spreadsheets by Monday EOD:
   - "Baseline (2x A10G equiv)" with expected p50/p95 token latencies for 256/512/1k contexts and concurrency 1/5/10/18.
   - "Burst plan" showing how devoting an extra GPU affects throughput and cost per 1000 tokens.
2) Monica: draft a 3-bullet SOW for a 30-day pilot (objectives, success criteria, pricing band).
3) Confirm region: us-west-2; mention any cross-region failover implications in the deck.
4) Bring a short set of fallback recommendations (model variant + lower quantization) if Vertex cannot meet latency targets on first pass.

Also flag: Alex called out Black Friday burst — include a note about pre-warming/auto-burst policies.

I’ll pull together a 10-minute agenda and share the meeting invite details and Dial-in in the morning.

—Lauren
